exampleAnswers.title: Evaluating the Limit of a Square Root Function

question.explanation:
The function $\sqrt{12x^{2} + 1}$ is well defined for $x \in (-\infty,\infty),$ and so to find this limit we substitute $x=2$ into the above expression:

\begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x \to 2} \sqrt{12x^{2} + 1}&= \sqrt{12\cdot 2^{2} + 1} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{49} \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{7} \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating the Limit of a Square Root Function

question.explanation:
Let $f(x)= \sqrt{x-4}.$ Notice that

\begin{align*} f(4) &= \sqrt{4 - 4}\\[3pt] &= \sqrt 0 \\[3pt] &= 0. \end{align*}

Let's sketch the graph of $y=f(x)\mathbin{:}$

From the graph, we notice that for the left-hand limit, we have

\[ \lim_\limits{x \to 4^-} f(x) = \textrm{DNE} \]

For the right-hand limit, we have:

\[ \lim_\limits{x \to 4^+} f(x) = 0 \]

Since the two limits are not equal, we conclude that

\[ \lim_\limits{x \to 4} f(x)= \textrm{DNE}. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Evaluating a Limit at Infinity of a Square Root Function

question.explanation:
Let $f(x)= \sqrt{-3x+8}.$ Let's sketch the graph of $y=f(x)\mathbin{:}$

From the graph, we see that the function increases without bound as $x$ decreases. Therefore,

\[ \lim_\limits{x \to -\infty} f(x)= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\infty}. \]

example.title: Evaluating a Limit at Infinity of a Square Root Function

question.explanation:
Let $f(x) = \sqrt{5-x}.$ Let's sketch the graph of $y = f(x){:}$

We see that the function is not defined for $x \gt 5.$ Therefore, \[ \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} f(x) = \textrm{DNE}. \]

example.title: Evaluating a Limit at Infinity of a Square Root Function

question.explanation:
Let $f(x)= \sqrt{x}.$ Let's sketch the graph of $y=f(x)\mathbin{:}$

We see that the function is not defined for $x \lt 0.$ Therefore,

\[ \lim_\limits{x \to -\infty} f(x)= \text{DNE}. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Evaluating the Limit of a Cube Root Function

question.explanation: We substitute $x = -3$ into the expression, and get \begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x \to -3} \sqrt[3]{7x-6} & = \sqrt[3]{7(-3)-6} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt[3]{-27} \\[3pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{-3}. \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating the Limit of a Cube Root Function

question.explanation:
We substitute $x=-3$ into the expression, and get

\begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x \to \left(-3\right)} \sqrt[3]{3x+9}&= \sqrt[3]{3(-3)+9} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt[3]{0} \\[5pt] &= 0. \end{align*}

question.explanation:
Let $f(x)= \sqrt[3]{-6-3x}.$ Let's sketch the graph of $y=f(x)\mathbin{:}$

From the graph, we see that the function decreases without bound as $x$ increases. Therefore, \[ \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} f(x)= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{-\infty}. \]
